scenario: AITA for disagreeing with our HR? | I am a 7 month newly hired employee for a big corporation. Last night our HR sent out a five page memo to all employees titled "Office Discipline". Basically, they were reminding everyone of the various rules around the office. Like not loitering during office hours, sticking to our lunch schedules, the correct dress code, wearing of IDs at all times etc. In my 6 month stay here our HR hasn't issued me an office ID card. Despite their large number of employees (they have an entire floor to themselves unlike multiple departments in one floor), they are slow. They took about 5 months to process my payroll alone, so the delay in ID cards are not a surprise to us. Everyone without an office ID just started using government issued IDs to be able to enter our building but this morning, security started telling everyone that starting next week anyone without an ID will have their names be noted and be reported to HR. I promptly called HR when I got to my desk to ask for a status for my (and my other colleagues) ID. They told me that they can't print our IDs yet because the team in charge is swarmed with other "projects" and suggested that we can print our own IDs, and gave us the template. My colleagues and I disagreed with this. We argued that we don't want to make up for the short comings of HR, by shelling out money from our own pockets to print our IDs, and that it should have been provided to us in the first place. We plan on just keep using whatever IDs we have right now be damned whatever happens next week. So, AITA for disagreeing with our HR?

Okay, let me try to figure out this AITA question. So the user is a new employee at a big corporation, 7 months in. HR sent a memo about office discipline, including wearing IDs. But the user hasn't received their ID yet, even after 6 months. The HR said they can't print IDs because the team is busy with other projects and suggested employees print their own using a template. The user and colleagues are refusing to pay for their own IDs and plan to keep using government IDs, ignoring HR's threat to report them.

First, I need to recall what AITA means. It's "Am I The Asshole?" where people post scenarios to get opinions on whether they're in the wrong. The answer is usually 0 (not asshole) or 1 (asshole).

So, analyzing the situation. HR is enforcing a rule that requires IDs, but they haven't provided them to employees. The company's own HR is at fault for not issuing IDs, which is a basic requirement for security. Employees shouldn't have to bear the cost of something the company should provide. If HR expects employees to print their own IDs, that's unfair because the company is responsible for supplying necessary work equipment or identifiers. Especially since the payroll was delayed for 5 months, which shows HR is slow, so it's not the employees' fault.

The employees are using government IDs as a temporary measure, which is reasonable. Security is now threatening to report them, but the problem is HR's failure to provide the IDs. So the employees are right to refuse paying for their own IDs. They shouldn't be penalized for HR's inefficiency.

But wait, maybe HR has a policy that IDs must be printed by employees? But that seems unlikely. Typically, companies provide IDs. If the company's policy says HR provides them, then HR's suggestion to print their own is wrong. If the company policy says employees have to pay for them, but that's unusual for a corporation. Usually, companies cover the cost of ID cards.

In most companies, especially large ones, ID cards are provided by the company as part of onboarding. So HR's suggestion to print their own is probably a bad move on their part. Therefore, the employees are justified in refusing to pay for them. They shouldn't be the ones to cover the cost because HR failed to do their job.

So, the answer should be 0, not the asshole. Because the responsibility lies with HR to provide the IDs, not the employees. So disagreeing with HR is correct here.

Wait, but maybe there's a legal aspect. In some places, maybe companies can require employees to pay for replacement IDs, but initial ones are usually free. But in this case, the employee is new and hasn't received the ID at all. So it's a basic onboarding item. So HR should have provided it. If they didn't, it's their fault, not the employee's.

So the employees are right to refuse to pay. Therefore, AITA? No, they're not the asshole. So answer is 0.
